slots.text: Gathers force gradually, reaching its peak around the sunset ritual.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Cavo Paradiso
slots.text: The cliffside open-air club above Paradise Beach, booking international DJs since 1993.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Jackie O' Beach Club
slots.text: Carries a poolside lunch into early-evening drag.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: The Garden
slots.text: On a hillside property that Yehudi Menuhin acquired after visiting in 1962; the music stays low enough for conversation.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Lío
slots.text: The full-night choice: an à la carte meal built around modern cabaret before becoming a club at 12:30 a.m.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: A sunrise run through the city
slots.text: A 5 or 10K running tour with Running in Morocco takes in the kasbah walls, Bab Agnaou and the Mamounia gates, adapted to your pace.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: The medina with a cultural guide
slots.text: Walk with Najat Noudari past breadmakers, blacksmiths, weavers and tanners, and landmarks like the Koutoubia Mosque and the Saadian Tombs.
slots.food: Lunch at La Table du Souk: prawn green salads and barbecue sea bass.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Odette Rooftop Bar
slots.text: A mezze menu of Moroccan ingredients with global flair, such as crispy sheep cheese cigars, and cocktails like Rock the Kasbah.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: A hot-air balloon at sunrise
slots.text: Drift above olive groves, desert ridges and Berber villages with Atlas Montgolfière, then land for a traditional desert-camp breakfast.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Bahia Palace and Dar Si Said
slots.text: A 19th-century marvel of painted ceilings and sculpted gardens, then a former palace holding Morocco's richest wood carvings and textiles.
slots.food: Lunch at Terrasse des Épices, or Zeitoun Cafe for lamb tagine and harira.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: El Fenn rooftop
slots.text: A design oasis beside the Koutoubia Mosque, pouring outstanding drinks like the El Pacha and cooking amazing meat and fish.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Jardin Majorelle
slots.text: Dreamed up in the 1920s by Jacques Majorelle and restored by Yves Saint Laurent and Pierre Bergé: a two-and-a-half-acre oasis in Majorelle Blue.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Yves Saint Laurent Museum
slots.text: Africa's first fashion museum, next door; book the combined ticket in advance.
slots.food: Post-museum lounging on the sun-drenched terrace café.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: A Royal Hammam
slots.text: La Sultana's Royal Hammam Signature treatment: a black-soap exfoliation, a body mask and gentle stretching.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: A local-led food tour
slots.text: Sample bun cha, bo la lot and endless varieties of che, sitting streetside on plastic stools.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Hoan Kiem Lake
slots.text: The Lake of the Returned Sword: stroll to the scarlet Huc Bridge and Ngoc Son Temple, a 19th-century shrine.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: The Alchemist and Beer Street
slots.text: A drink at speakeasy-style The Alchemist, then Ta Hien Street, nicknamed Beer Street, and Polite & Co.
slots.food: Dinner at Gia or Home Hanoi for elevated northern Vietnamese cuisine.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Su Quan Roastery
slots.text: A roughly two-hour workshop on traditional Vietnamese coffee, and turning it into egg coffee or coconut coffee.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Temple of Literature
slots.text: Vietnam's first university, founded in 1070, then the 11th-century Quan Thanh Temple.
slots.food: Lunch at Binh Banh My, a local recommendation.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Tran Quoc Pagoda
slots.text: The city's oldest Buddhist shrine, on West Lake, with scarlet towers that make a picture-perfect sunset.
slots.food: Dinner at Pho Suong: a cash-only stall famous for beef pho.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Hoa Lo Prison
slots.text: Nicknamed the Hanoi Hilton, where Vietnamese revolutionaries and U.S. POWs were imprisoned.
slots.food: Breakfast: coffee and banh mi in the Old Quarter.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Imperial Citadel of Thang Long
slots.text: A UNESCO World Heritage Site that was the political heart of Vietnam for more than a millennium.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Train Street
slots.text: Cafés and homes sit inches from a 19th-century railway; night trains typically pass around 7 and 9.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: An architecture walk in Brera
slots.text: A Context Travel tour of Milan's most important buildings, with a peek into vintage couture shop Cavalli e Nastri.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Pinacoteca di Brera
slots.text: An impressive Renaissance gallery, home to the 250-plus-year-old Accademia di Belle Arti di Brera.
slots.food: Aperitivo in the garden of Bvlgari Hotel Milan's Il Bar.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Voce Aimo e Nadia
slots.text: Dinner in the Galleria d'Italia, with changing tasting menus designed around the adjacent gallery's displays.
slots.food: Milan's iconic saffron risotto.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Triennale Milano
slots.text: Milan's design museum, with the newly opened Museo del Design Italiano permanent exhibit.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Fondazione Prada
slots.text: A sprawling 200,000-square-foot contemporary art complex with a nine-story tower and Wes Anderson's Bar Luce.
slots.food: Lunch at Terrazza Triennale: cacio e pepe and costoletta alla milanese.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Nebbia
slots.text: Part of a new generation of trattorias, with innovative takes on regional recipes in a minimalist space.
slots.food: Roasted pumpkin with goat milk and sesame, and a semifreddo dessert.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Via Montenapoleone
slots.text: One of Europe's most expensive shopping streets, then Via Spiga and Nilufar Gallery, a top design dealer.
slots.food: Breakfast at Pasticceria Cova: a cappuccino and pastry beneath chandeliers.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Maroncelli and 10 Corso Como
slots.text: The Maroncelli District is the latest enclave of boutiques, galleries and studios, near the 10 Corso Como concept store.
slots.food: Lunch at AMOR: the Alajmo brothers' patented steamed pizza.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Piazza del Duomo
slots.text: A gothic cathedral with 3,400 statues, beside Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II and its boutiques.
slots.food: A spritz on the Terrazza Aperol.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Sultan Qaboos Grand Mosque
slots.text: Over 90 acres, with a 164-foot central dome, a Swarovski chandelier and the world's second-largest carpet.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Mutrah Souq
slots.text: A traditional market built in the 1820s, with labyrinthine lanes for frankincense and khanjar, then the nearly two-mile Mutrah Corniche.
slots.food: A cup of karak, and Omani halwa with cardamom and saffron.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Royal Opera House Muscat
slots.text: A guided tour of Islamic, Mughal, Oriental and European influences, with rare instruments and landscaped gardens.
slots.food: Dinner at Hakkasan: contemporary Cantonese, starting with the Supreme dim sum.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: The Damaniyat Islands
slots.text: A 40-minute speedboat from Al Mouj Marina to nine limestone islands and coral reefs, a nature reserve ideal for snorkeling.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Guerlain Spa
slots.text: At The St. Regis Al Mouj: arrive early for the sauna and hammam, then an Imperial Relaxing Massage on a heated bed.
slots.food: Lunch at Zorba: breezy Greek food with sea vistas.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Coya
slots.text: Incan-heritage-inspired interiors and modern Peruvian food, best enjoyed family-style.
slots.food: The ceviche platter, prawn and sea bass gyoza, and tres leches cake.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Nizwa Fort
slots.text: Built over 12 years in the 17th century, with the largest circular tower in the region and notches for pouring hot date syrup on invaders.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Nizwa Souq
slots.text: Thought to date to the 3rd century, selling frankincense, silver jewelry, khanjar and pottery. Bargaining is expected.
slots.food: Lunch at Liwan Nizwa: rice with curried fish and grilled seafood.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Roberto's
slots.text: Contemporary Italian seafood at the hotel, starting with a frankincense-infused Spritz My Way.
slots.food: Slow-roasted octopus, and a pistachio ice cream with olive oil.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Midosuji Avenue
slots.text: Considered the Champs-Élysées of Osaka, and a favourite of travellers who like luxury shops.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Afternoon tea at The St. Regis Osaka
slots.text: On the 12th-floor rooftop Zen garden, with a seasonal Japanese sake garden.
slots.food: A traditional afternoon tea service, and the signature champagne sabrage at dusk.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Dotonbori
slots.text: A district that buzzes at all hours, with the famous Glico man advertisement, then Shinsaibashi's covered arcade.
slots.food: Okonomiyaki at Okonomiyaki Mizuno, crab at Kani Doraku or kitsune udon at Dotonbori Imai Honten.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Osaka Castle
slots.text: A reconstruction of the original with a museum-style attraction inside; book tickets online to skip the line.
slots.food: Breakfast at The St. Regis Osaka: a Japanese tray of soy-glazed fish, rice and tofu.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Sumiyoshi Taisha
slots.text: One of the oldest Shinto shrines in Japan, founded in the third century, with the iconic Sorihashi Bridge.
slots.food: Or catch a bunraku show at the National Bunraku Theatre.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Teppanyaki Wajo
slots.text: A high-end grill with seafood from the Seto Inland Sea and beef from Kobe, led by a chef who apprenticed under Joël Robuchon.
slots.food: Finish with a matcha green tea service.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Kuromon Market
slots.text: Dating back hundreds of years, with fresh seafood and meat, grilled seafood and yakitori skewers.
slots.food: Don't miss the takoyaki, round savory bites usually filled with octopus.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: A day trip to Nara
slots.text: Pay respect to the almost 50-foot bronze Buddha at Tōdai-ji, among the many deer roaming local sites.
slots.food: Kyoto, under an hour by train, is the other option.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Kobe beef
slots.text: Kobe is the day trip for foodies, with many excellent restaurants serving the region's marbled beef.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: KR Market Flower Lanes
slots.text: Wake at 4.30 or 5 a.m. and walk into lanes that smell of jasmine, marigold and incense, where the city buys its flowers.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Lalbagh Botanical Garden
slots.text: The slightly more serious cousin of Cubbon: a botanical garden, an ornamental lake and that iconic glasshouse.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Church Street crawl
slots.text: The stretch connecting MG Road and Brigade Road, packed with cafés, bookshops, brews and bars.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Cubbon Park
slots.text: If Bengaluru had lungs, this would be it: come early and see runners, dogs, yoga classes and power-walking uncles.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Bengaluru Palace
slots.text: The slightly royal part of the day: a Tudor-style structure built by the Wadiyars.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Commercial Street
slots.text: Where Bengaluru has shopped for years, still the place for street fashion, export surplus and jutti.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Malleshwaram mural walk
slots.text: Old Bengaluru in textbook form: conservancy lanes, trees, and a street art trail called Malleshwaram Hogona.
slots.food: Breakfast on the classic darshini trail: dosa or idli, steel plate in hand, in a crowded darshini.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Visvesvaraya Museum and the Aquarium
slots.text: Right next to Cubbon Park, a very specific kind of childhood nostalgia for science and aquariums.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: NGMA Bengaluru
slots.text: Modern Indian art and international exhibitions in a beautiful old mansion with a leafy courtyard.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: National Museum
slots.text: The mother of all museums in Delhi, with a collection spanning five thousand years of history.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: National Gallery of Modern Art
slots.text: In the heart of Lutyens' Delhi, with over 17,000 artworks, the largest repository of modern and contemporary art.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Lodhi Garden
slots.text: A 90-acre park in the centre of Delhi, housing tombs dating back to the late Delhi Sultanate.
slots.food: Dinner at Kwality Restaurant in the Regal building, serving Delhi since 1940.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Dhoomimal Art Gallery
slots.text: Established in 1936, widely regarded as one of the country's oldest private art galleries.
slots.food: Breakfast at Wenger's: a bakery established in 1926 by a Swiss couple.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: State Emporia Complex
slots.text: An Indian handicrafts goldmine on the edge of Baba Kharak Singh Marg, built after Independence.
slots.food: Lunch at Kake da Hotel: famous for its butter chicken.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: My Bar Headquarters
slots.text: Always in the thick of after-hours: the epitome of the neighbourhood dive bar.
slots.food: Dinner at Kikli: a restored haveli serving chef Amninder Sandhu's family Punjabi recipes.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Sunder Nursery
slots.text: A 16th-century restored heritage park complex spread across 90 acres.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Gandhi Memorial Museum
slots.text: More of a memorial than a conventional museum, with artefacts and impressions from Mahatma Gandhi's life.
slots.food: Lunch at Indian Coffee House, a slow, democratic city veteran.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Ikk Panjab
slots.text: Vibrant colours, dark mahogany furniture and pre-Partition aesthetics, with excellent food to match.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Gateway of India
slots.text: Right opposite the Taj Mahal Palace, the perfect starting point for exploring old Bombay.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Art-Deco Mumbai walk
slots.venue: Bombay High Court & the Oval Maidan
slots.text: A tour of one of Asia's largest collections of Art Deco architecture, the UNESCO World Heritage cluster around Oval Maidan.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Marine Drive
slots.text: Not cheesy but rightfully dazzling: the Queen's Necklace, beside a sprawling heritage Art Deco cluster.

days.title: Poetry, food and a dive bar

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Bombay Poetry Crawl
slots.text: A walking tribute to the city's most renowned poets, from the spaces they wrote in to the subjects of their poetry.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Mumbai Food Tour
slots.text: A voyage through Mumbai's culinary history with over 15 food-tasting stops, run by A Chef's Tour.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Woodside Inn
slots.text: One of the top picks for nightlife in a city where drinks come for every tax bracket.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Mumbai Bazaar Walk
slots.text: A walking tour of the native bazaars, including Phool Galli, the Jama Masjid area and Zaveri Bazaar.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Kitab Khana
slots.text: The city's most coveted independent bookstore, in a 150-year-old colonial building.
slots.food: Britannia is one of the city's cherished Irani cafés, worth a solo visit.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Hill Road
slots.text: Ask any Mumbaikar: for shopping, Hill Road is better.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Gangaramaya Buddhist Temple
slots.text: A Buddhist holy place that is also home to a museum and gallery, a place to find your centre in a hectic city.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Jami-Ul-Alfar Mosque
slots.text: A striking candy-striped mosque in a busy commercial district.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Galle Face Green
slots.text: A beachfront urban park favoured by local families, with a promenade made for strolling.
slots.food: Tea and scones on the colonial-era verandah of the Galle Face Hotel.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Geoffrey Bawa's Number 11
slots.text: The well-preserved home of one of Asia's greatest architects, for architecture and design fans.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Nelum Pokuna Art Street
slots.text: A hot spot for Colombo's up-and-coming artists, with affordable art to take home.
slots.food: Lunch at Café Kumbuk: light dishes made with local, seasonal, organic ingredients.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: The Cricket Club Café
slots.text: A cricket-themed bar and café with a nifty collection of cricketing memorabilia.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Sri Kailawasanathan Swami Kovil
slots.text: A Hindu temple with a façade and roof adorned with ornate statues of gods and goddesses.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Thusare Talking Hands
slots.text: A massage service run by vision-impaired locals, for long-haul and backpack-weary muscles.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Eat, Eat and Repeat tour
slots.text: A small-group walking tour that reveals Colombo's best street eats.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall
slots.text: A large, ornate hall within a huge cultural precinct and a cherry blossom-filled garden.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Taipei 101 Observatory
slots.text: The impossible-to-miss 508-metre-tall tower.
slots.food: Lunch at Din Tai Fung: Michelin-starred and surprisingly affordable dumplings.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Elephant Mountain
slots.text: A popular hiking trail and vantage point, for sunset over the city with the illuminated Taipei 101.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Xinyi Eslite Bookstore
slots.text: Taiwan's largest bookstore, four storeys and 8000 square meters: an oasis for book nerds and stationery lovers.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Red House
slots.text: An octagonal cultural centre in Ximending, a weekend market and a hub for art and design.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Ximending
slots.text: Taipei's youth culture and alternative fashion centre, often dubbed little America.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Jiufen
slots.text: A magical, lantern-lit town that inspired the film Spirited Away.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Taroko Gorge National Park
slots.text: One of Taiwan's largest national parks, if you want a longer day trip from Taipei.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Shilin Night Market
slots.text: One of Taiwan's bustling night markets, where generations of families have gone to eat, drink and socialise.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Hofburg Palace
slots.text: The beating heart of the Austro-Hungarian empire, and today the official residence of the Austrian president.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Walk the Ringstrasse
slots.text: Wrapped around the historic city centre, the Ring is the result of a Habsburg emperor's grand redevelopment.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Palmenhaus
slots.text: In the Burggarten by the Hofburg, quite possibly the world's grandest greenhouse, and a place to dine.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: The Kiss at Belvedere Palace
slots.text: Klimt's The Kiss, the final painting of his Golden Period, is the centrepiece of the world's most significant Klimt collection.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Wien Museum
slots.text: The free-to-enter museum at Karlsplatz finally reopened in late 2023 after an extensive revamp.
slots.food: Try Vienna's signature cake, the Sachertorte: dense chocolate sponge and dark chocolate ganache.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: A Schanigarten
slots.text: A typical Viennese phenomenon: a small open space in front of a restaurant, for a hot summer's day or night.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Café Central
slots.text: Vienna's most venerable café, opened in 1876, which commands a queue to rival any London hotspot.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Sigmund Freud Museum
slots.text: Freud lived and worked at Berggasse 19 until 1938, when the Nazis' persecution drove him from the city.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: MuseumsQuartier
slots.text: MQ offers everything from the world's finest Egon Schiele collection to a lively courtyard.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Buda Castle
slots.text: A short funicular climb from Clark Ádám tér takes you to the former royal palace atop Castle Hill.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Zugliget Chairlift
slots.text: Glide up to Budapest's highest point, János Hill at 527 metres, in 12 panoramic minutes.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Glide along the Danube
slots.text: The river defines Budapest, dividing it into Buda and Pest, and is linked by a series of bridges.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: New York Café
slots.text: Budapest's most elegant coffeehouse of the 1890s has regained its status after conversion into a five-star hotel.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: House of Terror
slots.text: The house at Andrássy út 60 was headquarters of the Communist Secret Police.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Szimpla Kert
slots.text: Budapest's original ruin bar, in a vast, dilapidated building, which set the tone for the rest.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Széchenyi Baths
slots.text: An ornate oasis of relaxation in thermal waters, surrounded by the greenery of City Park.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Budapest's murals
slots.text: Numerous firewalls around Pest, particularly in District VII, are decorated with murals, some related to Hungarian history.
slots.food: Lunch at Time Out Market Budapest, a food and cultural hub under one roof.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: A38 Boat
slots.text: A former Ukrainian stone-carrying cargo ship, now one of Budapest's most popular nightspots for live music.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: The Glockenspiel
slots.text: In Marienplatz, a famous clock depicts events from the city's history with the help of 43 bells.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Viktualienmarkt
slots.text: An open-air food market dating back over 200 years, a handy and relatively inexpensive pit stop.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Glockenbachviertel
slots.text: The once-edgy heart of Munich's LGBTQ+ scene, now gentrifying but still vibrant.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Olympiapark
slots.text: A colossal park originally built for the 1972 games, home to several attractions.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Eisbach surfers
slots.text: Surfing seems an unlikely sight in a landlocked city, but watch surfers master the main wave in the Eisbach.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Müllersches Volksbad
slots.text: An impressive indoor pool on the banks of the river, open since 1901 with many original features.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Munich's museums for €1
slots.text: Many of Munich's fabulous museums reduce their admission fee to one euro on Sundays.
slots.food: Breakfast at Bageri, the city's smallest and most unusual bakery.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Haus der Kunst
slots.text: A structure built for Nazi-approved art in 1937, now with a cutting-edge programme of events and exhibitions.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Kosmos unter N
slots.text: A pop-up beer garden that's anything but traditional, below street level on a construction site in Schwabing.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Angkor Wat
slots.text: The most iconic of Angkor's many temples, best experienced at sunrise.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Angkor Thom
slots.venue: The faces of the Bayon at Angkor Thom
slots.text: The ancient walled capital of the Khmer empire; the name literally translates as Great City.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Old Market
slots.venue: The Old Market (Psar Chas) and Pub Street, framed
slots.text: The place for cheap souvenirs and great street food.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Ta Prohm
slots.text: A temple half-devoured by the jungle, where Tomb Raider was filmed.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: More Angkor temples
slots.text: An attempt to visit as many of the stone wonders as possible; you're unlikely to see them all.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Phare Ponleu Selpak
slots.text: A Cambodian circus that helps the community, combining traditional dance, circus arts and performance.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Cooks in Tuk Tuks
slots.text: A Khmer cooking school where students shop for groceries at a market, then cook a traditional meal.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Kandal Village
slots.text: The best spot for socially conscious shopping and great coffee, far from the chaotic Old Market.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Miss Wong
slots.text: A classy cocktail bar with good music and relaxed vibes.
slots.food: Sombai: the best place to sample locally made Sraa Tram, a traditional soaked wine.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Sky Tower
slots.text: Looming over the city at 328 metres, Auckland's most iconic building, with 360-degree views.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Auckland Art Gallery
slots.venue: Auckland Art Gallery Toi o Tāmaki
slots.text: Home to more than 18,000 artworks, with the world's largest permanent collection of New Zealand art.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Maungawhau / Mount Eden
slots.text: Auckland's tallest and most-visited volcanic peak: the name means mountain of the whau tree.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Auckland Museum
slots.venue: Auckland War Memorial Museum (Tāmaki Paenga Hira)
slots.text: The city's leading, and free, museum, with a special insight into Māori culture and New Zealand's history.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: The Big Foody food tour
slots.text: More than 15 years of introducing travellers to Auckland's food, led by foodie Elle Armon-Jones.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Ponsonby Road
slots.text: A trendy strip for eating, drinking, shopping and people-watching.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Ōmanawanui Track
slots.text: An epic 3.7-kilometre coastal hike in the Waitakere Ranges of West Auckland.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: E-bike tour
slots.text: The best way to see Auckland is on two wheels: guided e-bike tours past the city's landmarks.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: All Blacks Experience
slots.text: More than a museum: an immersive experience honouring the black jersey, where you can test your rugby skills.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Kawarau bungy jump
slots.venue: Kawarau Bridge Bungy: the World's First
slots.text: The original and best bungy jump experience, at the home of bungy jumping, founded by AJ Hackett.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Shotover Jet
slots.text: A breathtaking jet boat ride through the Shotover River canyons, with 360-degree turns.
slots.food: Lunch at Ferg Burger: the famous burger joint, with a line at any time.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Skyline Queenstown
slots.text: A gondola ride up the mountain, with activities and dining at the summit and killer views.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Queenstown Wine Trail
slots.text: A family-owned wine touring company, with personalised and group experiences through Central Otago.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Arrowtown
slots.text: An historic gold rush village on the Arrow River, about 20 minutes' drive from Queenstown.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Botswana Butchery
slots.text: A meat-lover's paradise in the historic Archer's Cottage, with lake views.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Ziptrek Ecotours
slots.text: Guided zip-line tours through the treetops of Queenstown, for the joy of zooming through the trees.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Mountain biking
slots.text: Hilly bike trails for all levels of riders, for fresh air and some fun.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Jack's Point golf
slots.text: A scenic golf course less than half an hour from downtown Queenstown.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: St Peter's Abbey and Catacombs
slots.text: Free to enter and an interesting place to mooch about, with a graveyard and catacombs.
slots.food: Breakfast at Stiftsbäckerei St. Peter: the oldest bakery in Salzburg, still baking organic bread, next to a water mill.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Mirabell Palace
slots.text: A grand palace surrounded by lush, colourful gardens, where big scenes from The Sound of Music were shot.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Augustiner Bräu
slots.text: A traditional old beer house that brews its beer using a recipe perfected by the monks who founded the brewery.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Rudolf Budja Gallery
slots.text: Not just another gallery: it feels like viewing a private collection in someone's home.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Hangar-7
slots.text: A super-slick aircraft hangar owned by Red Bull co-founder Dietrich Mateschitz, full of eye-popping architecture.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Darwin's Bar
slots.text: A cosy bar in the new town, close to the river, especially good for cocktails in a laid-back atmosphere.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: 220 Grad
slots.text: A modern coffee and brunch spot with its own in-house roastery and a small lunch and brunch menu.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Balkan Grill Walter
slots.text: A take-away sausage shop in the old town: walk up to the window and order a hot sausage, a simple yet perfect affair.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Green Garden
slots.text: For a healthy and memorable meal when you've had your fill of wiener schnitzel and heavy dumplings.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Hallgrímskirkja
slots.text: Reykjavik's defining landmark and one of Iceland's most striking buildings: a soaring concrete church.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Harpa
slots.text: The second most famous landmark, on the waterfront: a concert hall and cultural centre.
slots.food: A hot dog from Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur, the most iconic stand in Iceland.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: The Old Harbour
slots.text: Reykjavik's historic harbour, from where guided whale-watching tours depart.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Golden Circle bus tour
slots.text: No trip to Iceland is complete without the famed Golden Circle, a popular tourist route.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Perlan
slots.text: Inside a gleaming glass dome on a hill above the city: part museum, part immersive nature experience.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Sky Lagoon
slots.text: Ten minutes from downtown in Kópavogur, the city's sleekest spot for a soak.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Settlement Exhibition
slots.text: A look at the early days of Reykjavik, where the excavated ruins sit on one side.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Tjörnin Pond
slots.text: A small lake in the heart of the city, fringed by colourful houses, City Hall and outdoor sculptures.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: A local outdoor pool
slots.text: Iceland is built on its swimming pools: every neighbourhood has one, deep and shallow.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Nice's Old Town
slots.text: Recognised by UNESCO in 2021, and more ancient than it seems, dating back to the third century BC.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Marché aux Fleurs Cours Saleya
slots.text: An incredible flower market in the Old Town dating back to 1897, with fruit and vegetables too.
slots.food: Lunch at Chez Theresa: a cute spot in the old town that specialises in socca.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Colline du Château
slots.text: Castle hill, where the medieval castle was destroyed by Louis XIV in 1706, for lovely views.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Musée Matisse
slots.text: Matisse lived in Nice for nearly 40 years, and this museum holds one of the world's largest collections of his work.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Promenade des Anglais
slots.text: A 7km paved promenade paid for by wealthy English expats who liked to wander the seafront.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Hotel Negresco
slots.text: A historic hotel on the Promenade, more than 100 years old, with a pastel-pink domed roof.
slots.food: A cocktail at the hotel bar.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Musée Terra Amata
slots.text: Nice has incredible prehistoric sites, even if they get skipped over for the famous beach clubs.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Specialty coffee tour
slots.text: Nice's new wave of baristas and roasters, who really know their beans.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Cave de la Tour
slots.text: Founded in 1947, one of the city's oldest wine bars, with local wines and varieties from across France.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Walk the City Walls
slots.text: The easiest and most popular itinerary for visitors: a stroll around the fortifications.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Rector's Palace
slots.text: The most historic monument in Dubrovnik, which was rebuilt twice.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Jazz at the Troubadour
slots.text: On any given night for six months of the year, crowds flock to this intimate enclosed square for outdoor jazz.
slots.food: Dinner at Nautika: calling itself Dubrovnik's finest restaurant, certainly the most prestigious.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Lokrum island
slots.text: An uninhabited isle on Dubrovnik's doorstep, unspoilt and lush with pines, palms and cypress trees.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: The cable car to Srđ
slots.text: The gleaming orange cable car scaling the steep incline above the old town.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: The cliff bars
slots.text: Far from the downtown flock, five minutes along a back alley, panoramic terraces for a beer.
slots.food: Dinner at 360: a Michelin-starred meal, perhaps the best in Croatia.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: The medieval pharmacy
slots.text: Of all the old town treasures, the Franciscan Monastery and its Old Pharmacy Museum are the real gems.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: The Red History Museum
slots.text: Croatia was part of the communist-ruled Yugoslav federation from 1945 until 1991.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Jadran open-air cinema
slots.text: An outdoor cinema nestled in the city walls, open all summer and owned by the city.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Qorikancha
slots.venue: Qorikancha (Temple of the Sun / Santo Domingo)
slots.text: The ruins of a once-grand sacred Incan temple, visible beneath the Church and Convent of Santo Domingo the Spanish built in the 1500s.
slots.food: Then Mercado San Pedro, Cusco's central market, for fruit juices and spices.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Museo Inka and Museo de Machu Picchu
slots.text: Two museums to prepare for Machu Picchu: Incan culture, and the world's largest collection of Machu Picchu artifacts.
slots.food: Lunch at Chicha, Gastón Acurio's Cusco outpost: cuy served like Peking duck, or alpaca carpaccio.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Organika
slots.text: A light supper where many ingredients come from their own Sacred Valley gardens, after a pisco sour lesson at the hotel.
slots.food: The tiradito de trucha with local trout and sweet potato chips.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Sacsayhuamán
slots.text: An archaeological site built in the 1400s above 12,000 feet, with walls of massive stone blocks fitted without mortar.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: San Blas
slots.text: Walk down stone staircases and lanes lined with colourful street art, with coffee or hot chocolate at Xapiri Ground.
slots.food: Lunch at Green Point: plant-based dishes in the garden, such as the Vegan Cusco Grill.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Planetarium Cusco
slots.text: A family-run star-gazing site with a presentation on the Incas' view of the cosmos and, weather permitting, a telescope.
slots.food: Finish with a pisco sour in the hotel bar.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Pisac Market
slots.text: The vibrant Sunday fair in the Sacred Valley town of Pisac, with handwoven textiles, Inca-inspired pottery and spit-roasted cuy.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Ollantaytambo Fortress
slots.text: The stone terraces of the Ollantaytambo fortress, one of the sights covered by Cusco's boleto turístico.
slots.food: Lunch at Mil, overlooking the Moray ruins and serving only what grows above 11,500 feet.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Museo del Pisco
slots.text: A slick bar with locations in Cusco, Lima and Arequipa, serving pisco sours and cocktails made with coca leaves and purple corn.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: A sidecar tour
slots.text: Porto Sidecar Tours offers guided rides from the sidecar of a vintage motorcycle, from the cathedral to the best coffee shops.
slots.food: Lunch: a francesinha at A Regaleira, widely credited as the home of the original.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Clérigos Church and São Francisco
slots.text: Climb roughly 225 spiral steps for panoramic views, then see the Church of Saint Francis, covered in gold leaf.
slots.food: A pastel de nata at C'alma Coffee Room.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: The Ribeira
slots.venue: The Ribeira & Cais da Ribeira riverfront
slots.text: A riverside promenade, with a white port and tonic as the light shifts over the Dom Luís I Bridge.
slots.food: Dinner at O Antunes: a family-owned restaurant for bacalhau and pork knuckle for two; reservations a must.

days.title: Cathedral, market and World of Wine

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Porto Cathedral and the Chapel of Souls
slots.text: Built in the 12th century with Gothic cloisters, then the Chapel of Souls, covered in blue-and-white azulejo tiles.
slots.food: Breakfast at Zenith: bacon-and-egg pancakes or avocado toast on charcoal-cocoa bread.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: World of Wine
slots.venue: WOW: World of Wine cultural district
slots.text: A sprawling complex in the old port wine warehouses of Vila Nova de Gaia, with seven museums and 12 restaurants.
slots.food: Lunch at Mercado do Bolhão: presunto, cheese, oysters and vinho verde from the market vendors.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Jardim do Morro
slots.text: A hilltop garden in Gaia with some of the city's best views of Porto and the Douro; arrive just before sunset.
slots.food: Dinner at Yeatman Gastronomic Restaurant: chef Ricardo Costa's tasting menus matched to the cellar.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: A Douro boat trip
slots.text: A boat trip along the Douro wine region is described as an absolute must, with sights, scenery and wine.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Livraria Lello
slots.text: One of the world's most beautiful bookstores, said to have inspired J.K. Rowling. A rite of passage for book lovers.
slots.food: Then Porto's traditional chocolate makers: Avianense, the oldest, from 1914, and Arcádia.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Cervejaria Gazela
slots.text: A counter in the Batalha neighbourhood famous for its cachorrinhos, a Portuguese hot dog.
slots.food: A toasted bun with sausage, melted cheese, butter and spicy sauce, cut into pieces.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Msheireb Museums
slots.text: Four restored heritage homes tracing Qatar's social, cultural and economic development, including Bin Jelmood House and Radwani House.
slots.food: Breakfast at IzuIzu on Baharat Msheireb: truffled eggs or avocado toast.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: National Museum of Qatar
slots.text: Designed by Jean Nouvel and inspired by the desert rose, with immersive exhibits on Qatar's history.
slots.food: Lunch at Jiwan: modern Qatari food with Alain Ducasse, on a terrace over the skyline.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Nobu Doha
slots.text: On its own private island at the Four Seasons, with a 360-degree rooftop terrace and the famed black cod.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Museum of Islamic Art
slots.text: An I.M. Pei building holding 1,200 years of Islamic history, including the rare Abbasid Blue Quran.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: The Mina District
slots.text: Cobblestone streets and pastel-coloured buildings, with cafés and vibrant street art murals.
slots.food: Lunch at Baron: whole-roasted cauliflower and capellini with crab and shrimp toum.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Souq Waqif
slots.text: A living market and the best attraction to leave for last, starting at the Falcon Souq.
slots.food: Dinner at Al Mourjan for classic Arabic dishes, or karak and chapati at Ali Al Naama.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Qanat Quartier at The Pearl
slots.text: A pastel, Venice-inspired shopping promenade along canals, with a replica Bridge of Sighs and piano stairs near Qanat Quartier 7.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Souq Al Wakrah
slots.text: A new construction on an old site of fishing and pearl diving, with sand-coloured buildings, winding lanes and a small domed mosque.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Boho Social
slots.text: A rooftop terrace in Katara Cultural Village with panoramas across West Bay and The Pearl Qatar, made for sunset.
slots.food: An eclectic, South American-centric menu.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Tailors and leather in Ancient Town
slots.text: A bespoke leather bag at Buffalo Leather Shop or a custom jacket at Sewing Bee Tailors, with a fitting booked for the next day.
slots.food: Coffee at Hoi An Roastery, served with sweetened condensed milk.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Central Market and the Japanese Covered Bridge
slots.text: Browse Central Market, then the Japanese Covered Bridge, Quan Cong Temple and the Old House of Tan Ky.
slots.food: Lunch at Banh Mi Phuong, which Anthony Bourdain called the best banh mi in Vietnam.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Ancient Town by lantern light
slots.text: At dusk, merchants switch off the electric lights and light silk lanterns; chilled wine at White Marble Wine Bar.
slots.food: Dinner at Nữ Eatery: avocado salad, pork belly buns, chili lime shrimp and lemongrass ice cream.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: A Vespa countryside tour
slots.text: On refurbished 1960s Italian scooters across the Thu Bon River to Cam Kim Island, with a boatyard, rice paddies and a coffee roasting lesson.
slots.food: A seafood feast on the beach to finish.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: An Bang Beach
slots.text: Two miles south of the hotel, with casual cafés serving cocktails, beer and live music.
slots.food: Or visit the Marble Mountains.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Miss Ly Café
slots.text: A charming family-run address with warm wood tables and ice-cold Tiger Beer.
slots.food: White rose dumplings and crispy cao lầu.

days.title: Cooking, assembly halls and the river

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Tra Que Gardens cooking school
slots.text: Walk the organic vegetable farm that supplies most good chefs in Hoi An, then make spring rolls, salads and peanut sauce.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Fujian Assembly Hall
slots.venue: Fujian Assembly Hall (Phuc Kien / Phuoc Kien)
slots.text: A Chinese hall built in 1690, with a shrine to Thien Hau, the sea goddess who protects sailors, and a colourful courtyard.
slots.food: Vietnamese coffee at Mia Coffee, or a banh mi at Madam Khanh's stall.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Bars on the Thu Bon River
slots.venue: Hoi An Ancient Town riverside bars
slots.text: The riverbank was once where traders drank between voyages. Try the local rice wine, or the beers at Hoi An Artisan.
slots.food: The Mango Chili Pale Ale or the Chocolate Mulberry Bock.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: The Spice and Gold Souks
slots.text: Cross the creek by abra to Deira's oldest markets: sacks of saffron and cardamom, then windows dressed in gold and diamonds.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Al Fanar Restaurant and Café
slots.text: An interior that transports you to 1960s Dubai, serving authentic Emirati food, before the Dubai Mall.
slots.food: Samboosa and hobool, then machboos deyay and leqaimat.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: At The Top, Burj Khalifa
slots.text: Go an hour before sunset for views from the observation deck on the 124th floor of the world's tallest skyscraper.
slots.food: Dinner at Zaroob: crispy falafel, creamy hummus and man'oushe.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Dubai Museum and Al Bastakiya
slots.text: Al Fahidi Fort, built in 1787, then the heritage district of Al Bastakiya, with teahouses, galleries and the XVA Art Hotel.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: The Sheikh Mohammed Centre
slots.text: A cultural lunch in House 26, with a local host to talk about Emirati culture and customs (reservations only).
slots.food: Traditional Emirati dishes, served at 1 p.m. Sunday to Thursday.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Dubai Opera
slots.text: A boat-shaped building nodding to the city's roots as a trading port, hosting international performances.
slots.food: Thai seafood at Thiptara by Burj Lake, with a view of the Dubai Fountain.

days.title: Museum of the Future, beach and Trèsind Studio

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Museum of the Future
slots.text: A stainless steel torus covered in Arabic calligraphy. Tickets sell out, but the exterior alone is worth a visit, by day or lit up at night.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Kite Beach
slots.text: A long-time residents' favourite with a running track, cycling path and boardwalk, clear swimmable water and sun beds to hire.
slots.food: Food trucks along the beach.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Trèsind Studio
slots.text: The world's only three-Michelin-starred Indian restaurant, seating just 20 diners in two nightly seatings, Monday to Saturday.
slots.food: Tasting menus that journey through regions of India, led by chef Himanshu Saini.

days.title: Temples, Old Town and street food

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Wat Chalong
slots.text: Phuket's largest and most important Buddhist temple, with a pagoda holding a splinter of bone from the Buddha. Go early and dress modestly.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Old Town and Chinpracha House
slots.text: Colourful old buildings and boutique shops along Soi Rommannee, then Chinpracha House, with its original family furnishings.
slots.food: Lunch at Mor Mu Dong in the Palai mangroves: the stuffed curried mackerel is a signature dish.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Chillva Night Market
slots.text: A bohemian market built from painted, upcycled shipping containers. Spend a couple of hours browsing and people watching.
slots.food: Eat your way around the stalls.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Phang Nga Bay and James Bond Island
slots.venue: James Bond Island (Khao Phing Kan / Koh Tapu)
slots.text: A speedboat day trip to the limestone cliffs made famous by 007, with a few smaller islands on the way.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Snorkelling and beach time
slots.text: The day trip adds small islands for quality snorkelling and relaxing beach time, before the boat heads back to Phuket.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Floating restaurants at Laem Hin Pier
slots.text: A free longtail boat takes five minutes from the pier to the floating restaurants near Coconut Island, and back beneath the stars.
slots.food: Oysters, crab, prawns and fish, cooked by traditional Thai methods.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Phuket Elephant Sanctuary
slots.text: An ethical sanctuary in Paklok, with no trick shows or rides. Feed the elephants and follow them as they roam.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Bangtao Beach
slots.text: An eight-kilometre stretch of soft white sand and turquoise water, with upscale beach clubs and restaurants.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Promthep Cape at sunset
slots.text: The southernmost point of Phuket, and its best sunset view. It gets very busy, so arrive early.
slots.food: For a quieter sundowner meal, wait for dark and book a table at the nearby Promthep Cape restaurant.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Museo Maya de Cancún
slots.venue: Museo Maya de Cancún & the El Rey ruins
slots.text: About 400 artifacts from across the Yucatán, in an air-conditioned museum. An archaeological site with temple remains sits just outside.
slots.food: Breakfast at Rooster, where locals go downtown for eggs benedict and avocado toast.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: El Rey Archaeological Zone
slots.venue: Museo Maya de Cancún & the El Rey ruins
slots.text: Small Mayan ruins in the Hotel Zone, easy to navigate, with views of the lagoon and a glimpse of Maya royal life.
slots.food: Lunch at El Fish Fritanga: ceviche tostadas, lobster tail or whole fried fish, on the sand by the lagoon.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Parque de las Palapas
slots.text: Come at sunset to the downtown park where Cancún locals gather, and watch people live their evenings.
slots.food: Mexican cakes, empanadas and cheesy treats from the stalls.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Isla Mujeres and Playa Norte
slots.text: A 20-minute ferry from Cancún. Rent a golf cart to explore the island, then claim some sand at Playa Norte.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Punta Sur
slots.text: The south end of the island has stunning cliff views and ziplining, or book a snorkelling excursion in turquoise water.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Navios
slots.text: Mexican fusion seafood served in romantic cabanas over the water, with a remarkable wine list.
slots.food: Try the robalo al pastor: sea bass carpaccio over pineapple with cilantro rice.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: MUSA underwater museum
slots.venue: MUSA: Museo Subacuático de Arte (underwater museum)
slots.text: More than 500 statues submerged in Cancún's marine park. Snorkel up close, or see them from a glass-bottomed boat.
slots.food: Coffee or hot chocolate at Ah Cacao Chocolate Café in La Isla Shopping Village.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Yum Cooking Workshop
slots.text: An afternoon class in the history of Mexican cuisine, then cooking, a six-course meal and a tequila tasting.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Coco Bongo
slots.text: Flying acrobats, pop star tributes and a party every night of the week. Tickets include unlimited drinks, so book ahead.
slots.food: Dine first at Chambao Fashion GrillHouse: smoking cocktails, surf and turf, and a fashion show.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Centro Cultural Banco do Brasil
slots.text: One of Rio's top cultural hubs, with stunning architecture and world-class exhibitions, worth visiting whatever is on.
slots.food: Then the recently opened Confeitaria Colombo, for the iconic Torrada Petrópolis.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Pequena África walking tour
slots.text: Walk through Saúde, Gamboa and Santo Cristo, where enslaved Africans first arrived in Brazil and a Black community remains.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Samba at Pedra do Sal
slots.text: Cap off the walk with samba at Pedra do Sal, held Friday through Monday evenings from 6pm.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Casa Firjan
slots.text: A French-style mansion in Botafogo that hosts talks on innovation, and houses Empório Jardim.
slots.food: Over 90 breakfast items; don't leave without the gruyère pão de queijo.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Santa Teresa tram
slots.text: Installed in 1872, the bondinho crosses the Arcos da Lapa and winds through the cobbled streets of Santa Teresa.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Mureta da Urca
slots.text: A one-kilometre seawall where young cariocas gather at golden hour, watching the sun set over Guanabara Bay.
slots.food: The shrimp pastel at Bar Urca, across the street.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Café 18 do Forte de Copacabana
slots.text: Breakfast with views over Copacabana Beach, from the fort at the end of the sand.
slots.food: The award-winning breakfast is served all day, with house-made pão de queijo da canastra.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Parque Lage
slots.text: The lush garden of a 19th-century mansion that is now the School of Visual Arts, known for its cultural events.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Armazém Cardosão
slots.text: A legendary spot for jazz and bohemian vibes in Laranjeiras, where Ney Conceição leads performances for a post-work crowd.
slots.food: Order the caipirinhas straight to your table.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Niederdorf
slots.text: The old town's narrow streets hold quirky shops and cosy bars. Visit Cabaret Voltaire, the cradle of Dada, or climb a Grossmünster tower for views.
slots.food: A porchetta roll and basque cheesecake at Ora Bar.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Kunsthaus Zürich
slots.text: Switzerland's largest art museum, with a room of Giacometti, Van Gogh, Monet and Chagall upstairs, and the largest Munch collection outside Norway.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Fondue at the Widder Garden
slots.text: Fondue at the Widder Garden, in four-cheese, truffle and champagne versions. In winter, eat inside a portable gondola.
slots.food: Book ahead for the gondola seatings.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Bahnhofstrasse
slots.text: One of the world's most expensive shopping streets: high street brands near the station, luxury shops towards the lake.
slots.food: Italian coffee at Bar 45, or the tourist-popular Café Sprüngli.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: FIFA Museum
slots.text: Rent a bike and ride to the history of the game, with interactive games to compete in.
slots.food: A beer at the former Hürlimann brewery, at B2 Boutique Hotel.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Kronenhalle
slots.text: Zurich's institution since 1924, with a dress code, warm service, strong cocktails and a private art collection on the walls.

days.title: Chocolate, Zurich West and a bar crawl

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Lindt Home of Chocolate
slots.text: On the shore of Lake Zurich, with a factory tour, the largest Lindt store in Switzerland and tempering masterclasses. Book ahead.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Zurich West
slots.text: Shops, restaurants and bars under the old railway viaduct, then Frau Gerolds Garten with its urban garden.
slots.food: Neapolitan-style pizza at Napule, a favourite of locals and Roger Federer.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: A bar crawl from Raygrodski
slots.text: Start with a cocktail at Raygrodski, move to COR Wine & Pintxos, and end at Bar 1838 for open-late dancing and views.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Jet d'Eau
slots.text: The fountain spouts 140m into the air. Shoot it from Pont du Mont-Blanc, or hop on a Mouette taxi-boat across the lake.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Old Town
slots.text: Wander around Cathédrale Saint-Pierre and Place du Bourg-de-Four, then see the archaeological remains beneath the cathedral.
slots.food: A break at Birdie Food and Coffee nearby.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Fondue at Les Armures
slots.text: A traditional setting for a top-flight caquelon of moitié-moitié, half gruyère and half vacherin.

days.title: Nations, the baths and fine dining

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Red Cross museum and Palais des Nations
slots.venue: International Red Cross & Red Crescent Museum
slots.text: The moving permanent exhibition on 150 years of humanitarian work, combined with a guided tour of the UN's European seat.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Bains des Pâquis
slots.text: A kitsch 1930s public bath on Lake Geneva, open year-round, for a dip, sauna or massage.
slots.food: Fondue or a cheap lunch in friendly, casual surroundings.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Arakel
slots.text: A modern French and Mediterranean kitchen, added to the 2026 Michelin Guide, among Geneva's daring, ambitious chefs.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Carouge
slots.text: A short tram ride away, an Italian-style quarter built by Turin settlers, with stone arches, glass blowers and bookshops.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: A chocolate tour
slots.text: The Choco Pass walks you through the best independent chocolatiers, including Guillaume Bichet, Favarger and La Maison du Rhône.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Rooftop at Le 105
slots.text: Rooftop views of the Jura mountains and Mont Salève in Lancy, where locals dance the night away.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Langkawi Cable Car and Sky Bridge
slots.text: One of the steepest cable cars in the world climbs about 1,700 metres to the top of Gunung Machinchang, with the Sky Bridge nearby.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Temurun Waterfall
slots.text: A trek up a three-tiered waterfall, with a natural pool at the top for a dip.
slots.food: Lunch at Siti Fatimah: the locals' lunchtime buffet of curries, seafood and stir-fries.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: The Cliff
slots.text: A bar on Pantai Cenang over the Andaman Sea, with sunsets to match, serving Malay and Western food.
slots.food: Sundowners and a Malay or Western dinner.

days.title: Sea, snorkelling and the night market

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Pulau Payar Marine Park
slots.venue: Pulau Payar Marine Park: Snorkelling & Diving
slots.text: A snorkelling tour with hotel pick-up and a boat out to a protected reef, with coral, colourful fish and sharks.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Helicopter over Dayang Bunting
slots.venue: Lake of the Pregnant Maiden (Tasik Dayang Bunting)
slots.text: A helicopter tour over Dayang Bunting Island and Lake Guillemard, the freshwater 'Lake of the Pregnant Maiden', best seen from above.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Kuah Night Market
slots.text: One of the best of Langkawi's pasar malam, with cheap souvenirs to bargain over and street food.
slots.food: Nasi ayam eaten amongst the throng.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Wat Koh Wanararm
slots.text: A modern Buddhist temple built into the hillside just outside Kuah, with grounds to wander. Entry is free.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Pantai Pasir Tengkorak
slots.text: A secluded beach with white sand and clear water backed by forest, frequented by monkeys, with toilets and showers on site.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Nest Rooftop
slots.text: A halal café-bar on a rooftop over Pantai Cenang, with regular gigs. It is booze-free, though you can bring your own for a small fee.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Coffea Coffee
slots.text: A cosy, wood-panelled café on Jalan Telawi 2 in Bangsar, known for the Madonna and Maestro lattes.
slots.food: Try the peanut butter latte or the green tea latte.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Bangsar
slots.text: A trendy former railway town, now known for its cafés, boutiques and restaurants. A good place for a latte, less for authentic Malaysian culture.
slots.food: Espressolab's outpost in the Times Bookstore at Bangsar Shopping Centre.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Cantaloupe
slots.text: On the 23rd floor of The Troika, with floor-to-ceiling windows and 360-degree views of the KL skyline.
slots.food: Fine de Claires oysters with marinated anchovy cream, or chorizo-dusted scallops.

days.title: Taman Tun Dr Ismail and Publika

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Artisan Roast
slots.text: The original shop in Taman Tun Dr Ismail, said to have spearheaded KL's independent coffee movement. No sugar or syrup allowed.
slots.food: Homemade muesli and cakes on the counter.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Taman Tun Dr Ismail
slots.text: A leafy, quiet suburb of artisanal cafés, cosy pubs and local hawkers, with an old-fashioned charm. Good for an afternoon of exploring.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: La Vie En Rose
slots.text: A distinguished fine-dining restaurant in a restored colonial house, serving classical French cuisine.
slots.food: Start with The Eiffel Tower champagne cocktail on the terrace, then the duck confit.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Publika
slots.text: A retail space with galleries and theatres open to the public. The original and best espressolab is tucked into its galleries.
slots.food: Coffee at espressolab.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Section 17
slots.text: A charming, quiet area just starting to attract hipsters, with excellent hawker food and restaurants such as Bistro a Table.
slots.food: Verona Trattoria for Italian.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Tamarind Springs
slots.text: An Indochinese restaurant in the rainforest of Ampang, with lantern-lit decking over the jungle.
slots.food: The Laotian coconut milk soup, or Phnom Penh-style wagyu beef lok lak.

days.title: Museum, old town and the Bund

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Shanghai Museum
slots.text: Start with the history of Shanghai at the city's museum.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Yuyuan Garden
slots.text: The old town around Yuyuan Garden, for traditional snacks and dim sum.
slots.food: Lunch of local snacks and dim sum in the old town.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: The Bund and a Huangpu cruise
slots.text: The Bund is a must-visit at night, and a cruise along the Huangpu River gives the best night view of Shanghai.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Jade Buddha Temple
slots.text: A temple for the history of Shanghai, to see in the morning with the city's attractions.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: The French Concession
slots.venue: The Plane-Tree Streets of the French Concession
slots.text: A walk through the French Concession, a very cosmopolitan part of the city.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Xintiandi
slots.text: Famous for its restaurants and bars, and the place for dinner.
slots.food: Try Mr & Mrs Bund for French, or Canton 8 for Chinese.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: West Lake
slots.text: An hour from Shanghai by bullet train, Hangzhou's West Lake has half-moon bridges and weeping willows.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Tea plantations and pagodas
slots.text: Tour the tea plantations, pagodas and temples around the lake before returning to Shanghai.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Speak Low
slots.text: Back in Shanghai, a drink at one of the city's great bars.
slots.food: Sober Company and Bar Rouge are other options.

days.title: Citadel, Al Balad and Rainbow Street

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Citadel Hill
slots.text: Wander among ruins that include the Umayyad Palace and the Roman-style Temple of Hercules, with 360-degree views of the city.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Al Balad and the Roman Theater
slots.text: The main street of old downtown for shopping, snacking and people-watching, then the restored 2nd-century Roman Theater.
slots.food: Kunafeh at the legendary Habibah.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Rainbow Street
slots.text: One of the oldest streets in Amman, quiet by day and alive in the evening, with galleries, shisha and cafés.
slots.food: Al Quds for the falafel sandwich, or sweets at Sufra.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Beit Sitti cooking class
slots.text: Cook with local chefs in a historic villa in Al Weibdeh, a legacy of three sisters' grandmother. Meals are on the terrace.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Al Weibdeh galleries and street art
slots.text: Browse Arab art at Darat Al Funun, Dar Al-Anda and The National Gallery of Fine Arts, and look for street art on the alleys and stairways.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: A rooftop sunset
slots.text: A city built on hills has plenty of sunset viewpoints. Reserve a rooftop terrace such as Cantaloupe Gastro Pub, Ghoroub or Wild Jordan.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Al Abdali and the blue mosque
slots.text: The 'new downtown', with The Boulevard's shops, steps from the King Abdullah I Mosque and its turquoise mosaic dome.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Iraq al-Amir
slots.text: About 10 miles out, with cliffside caves and the pre-Roman palace Qasr al-Abd, which is stunning at sunset.
slots.food: A meal prepared by the Iraq Al-Amir Women's Cooperative.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Kunafeh and umm Ali at Nasim
slots.text: A Bedouin-inspired setting at Fairmont Amman, for dessert after the day trip.
slots.food: Kunafeh, and the baked pastry pudding umm Ali.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Hanselmann and the town
slots.text: Explore the town on foot: Engadin houses with sgraffiti, art nouveau architecture and high-end boutiques.
slots.food: Hanselmann for nusstorte, hot chocolate and pretzels.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Lake St. Moritz
slots.text: The lookout, where kite surfers skim across the lake, though it's usually frozen from December to May.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: La Baracca
slots.text: A laid-back food shack and institution, across from the Kempinski, with a mix of ski instructors and late-night partiers.
slots.food: Polenta, carpaccio and salads, or fondue at Pichalain.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Muottas Muragl
slots.venue: Muottas Muragl: The Funicular & the Sunset
slots.text: Snowshoe or hike the low-mountain trail with a local guide, or learn to ski at one of the two ski schools.
slots.food: Lunch at La Terrazza on Corviglia in ski season, or Piz Nair in summer.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Segantini Museum
slots.text: Giovanni Segantini lived and worked in the Engadin for the last five years of his life, painting epic landscapes.
slots.food: Then the spa at Kempinski.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Cà d'Oro
slots.text: The most clever and fun of the top restaurants, with a non-run-of-the-mill Italian menu. Winter only.

days.title: Piz Nair, the glacier and a champagne bath

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Piz Nair
slots.venue: Corviglia & the Piz Nair Cable Car
slots.text: Reached by funicular and aerial tramway, at 10,030 feet, with stunning views.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Glacier Grotto on Corvatsch
slots.text: A journey up the summit of Corvatsch, rewarded with the natural beauty of the Glacier Grotto and Alpine lake and pasture views.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: A champagne bath and fondue
slots.text: Bathe in carbonated mineral water at Medizinisches Therapie Zentrum spa, then dinner in a converted farmhouse.
slots.food: Fondue at Chesa Veglia, in a rustic atmosphere.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: El Malecón
slots.text: A six-mile coastal path through several neighbourhoods, connecting green spaces and cafés with views of the Pacific.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Huaca Pucllana
slots.text: A pre-Inca pyramid in upscale Miraflores, built from vertically stacked adobe bricks to survive earthquakes. Visit the onsite museum.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Love Park
slots.text: A clifftop park along El Malecón, with mosaic walls and El Beso, a sculpture of kissing lovers by Víctor Delfín.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Dédalo Arte y Artesanía
slots.text: A mansion-turned-gallery showing Peruvian jewellery and furniture, with a brick courtyard café under an ancient ficus tree.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Jade Rivera World and street art
slots.venue: Casa Museo de Barranco murals & street art walk
slots.text: A gallery for the painter and muralist Jade Rivera, then Barranco's graffiti, including Bronik's women-centric murals.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: The Bridge of Sighs
slots.venue: Puente de los Suspiros (Bridge of Sighs)
slots.text: A wooden bridge from the 1870s. Local lore says that if you cross it holding your breath, your wish will come true.
slots.food: Street food such as anticuchos, then picarones for dessert.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Museo Larco
slots.text: Lima's most famous museum, packed with pre-Columbian ceramics, gold and silver vessels, and a collection of erotic pottery.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Olive Park
slots.text: A quieter green space in the financial district of San Isidro, with more than 1,600 olive trees, a pond and over 60 bird varieties.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Museo del Pisco
slots.text: A slick bar introducing Peru's brandy, with pisco sour variants and cocktails made with local ingredients.
slots.food: Or book a tasting-menu dinner at Astrid y Gastón, Central, Mayta or Maido.

days.title: The Matterhorn and the sun terraces

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Matterhorn Glacier Paradise
slots.text: A 45-minute gondola and cable car ride to Europe's highest cable car station, 3,883 metres up, with 38 four-thousanders in view.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Chez Vrony
slots.text: Locally sourced ingredients with a stunning backdrop of views to the Matterhorn.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: The Cervo sun terrace
slots.text: A big sun terrace with amazing views of the Matterhorn, where most of Zermatt gathers after the slopes. Live music.
slots.food: Alpine tapas.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Buffet Bar Sunnegga
slots.text: A self-service restaurant above Zermatt with standard mountain fare and one of the best angles of the Matterhorn.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Käsestube Furgg
slots.text: A traditional chalet-style restaurant with incredible views, perfect for a fondue, raclette or grilled cheese sandwich.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Brown Cow Pub
slots.text: A pub in the heart of the village, for après-ski.

days.title: Chocolate peaks, Italy and an open-air bar

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Bäckerei Fuchs
slots.text: A bakery known for its chocolate replicas of the famous peak.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Skiing to Italy
slots.text: Zermatt's ski area is the highest in Switzerland and links to Italy: ski over for a pasta lunch, then return for Swiss schnapps.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Hennu Stall
slots.text: A lively open-air spot for après-ski.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: The Pyramids and the Sphinx
slots.venue: The Pyramids of Giza & the Great Sphinx
slots.text: The pyramids are 2km from the city, and new hop-on-hop-off electric buses shuttle visitors around the three pyramids and the Sphinx.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Inside the Great Pyramid
slots.venue: The Pyramids of Giza & the Great Sphinx
slots.text: A hot, cramped crawl of about 100 metres to the empty King's Chamber, with only Khufu's sarcophagus. It takes about 15 minutes.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Sachi
slots.text: A sultry restobar in Heliopolis, part of a new nightlife scene of noteworthy cocktail menus in expat-heavy neighbourhoods and hip hotels.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Grand Egyptian Museum
slots.text: The largest archaeology museum in the world, with Tutankhamun's 5,000 objects, including his gold mask, and a 36-foot Ramses II in the atrium.
slots.food: On-site restaurants line the atrium for lunch.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: The Egyptian Museum
slots.text: The Tahrir Square museum still holds an impressive stock of Pharaonic antiquities.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Downtown ahwas
slots.text: The heart of Cairo's nightlife: cheap plastic chairs spill onto the streets outside all-night coffeehouses, for shisha, tea or coffee.

days.title: Old Cairo and a Zamalek rooftop

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Old Cairo
slots.text: A UNESCO-listed area of Biblical-era churches, medieval fortresses and the oldest synagogue in the world.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: The Museum of Egyptian Civilization
slots.venue: The National Museum of Egyptian Civilization (NMEC): the Royal Mummies
slots.text: The place to see the mummies of ancient Pharaohs.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Crimson
slots.text: A rooftop bar in Zamalek, with a noteworthy cocktail menu.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: The Pho Museum
slots.text: A three-storey museum in Ben Thanh Ward. A guided tour of 60 to 70 minutes traces pho's 100-year evolution, ending with a bowl.
slots.food: Each tour ends with pho and a local dessert.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Bến Thành Market alleys
slots.text: Wander the scooter-filled alleys around Bến Thành Market and eat on a tiny plastic stool on the nearest corner.
slots.food: Pho on your knees, or a crunchy banh mi on the fly.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Thu Thiem Peninsula
slots.text: Sunset over the Saigon River and the glittering skyscrapers, from the Thu Thiem Peninsula.
slots.food: Bun thit nuong, banh mi and com tam beforehand.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Antiques and Yersin Market
slots.text: Start early at Bún Riêu cua ốc Phan Rang, then Lê Công Kiều Street's antique dealers and the chaos of Yersin Market.
slots.food: Crab and snail noodle soup, then retro Hoàng Thị Cafe.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Museum of Fine Arts
slots.venue: Fine Arts Museum (Bao Tang My Thuat)
slots.text: Spend the afternoon at the Ho Chi Minh City Museum of Fine Arts.
slots.food: Lunch at Bếp Mẹ Ỉn for family-style dishes.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Madam Kew
slots.text: An opium-den-turned-cocktail-bar. Then bar-hop, starting at 419. Bar behind a vintage camera cabinet.
slots.food: Dinner at woodfire specialists Quince Eatery, downstairs.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Tân Định Market
slots.text: Behind the Disney-pink church, the ward is low-rise and peaceful. Browse the silk stalls of Tân Định Market.
slots.food: Steamed rice rolls at Bánh Cuốn Tây Hồ 127.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Cà Phê Đỗ Phủ
slots.text: A café where a wardrobe conceals a Tet Offensive bunker. Flip through Vietnamese vinyl at Hãng Đĩa Thời Đại.
slots.food: Charcoal-fired crêpes at Bánh Xèo 46A.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: PK Maltroom
slots.text: The country's first whisky bar, for a dram after dinner.
slots.food: Dinner at Ö by Hoang Tung.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Sodhani Sweets
slots.text: A sweet shop since 1954, packed from 6:30am for the brown, crackly pyaz kachoris dipped in tamarind chutney.
slots.food: A tall kulhad lassi and crispy jalebis.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: The Old City bazaars
slots.text: Walk through the terracotta pink gates, past spices, fruit, quilts and carpets, and stop for chai.
slots.food: Kachoris stuffed with unpeeled potatoes at Sampat Namkeen Bhandar, going since 1936.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: A stepwell evening
slots.text: Jaipur's long-neglected baolis are making a comeback, often doubling as atmospheric venues for traditional music and dance.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Anokhi Museum of Hand Printing
slots.text: A museum reviving ancient techniques, with block-printing sessions for visitors.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Museum of Meenakari Heritage
slots.text: Another museum refashioning ancient techniques into something that feels strikingly contemporary.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Spice Court
slots.text: A 1930s colonial mansion for no-nonsense Rajasthani cuisine, best known for keema baatis.
slots.food: Spicy slow-cooked laal maas with butter naan.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Amer Fort
slots.venue: Amber Fort (Amer Fort) & the Sheesh Mahal
slots.text: The fort where royals once lived, now with a heritage restaurant at its top.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: 1135 AD
slots.venue: 1135 AD at Amber Fort: royal dining
slots.text: A dreamy heritage restaurant atop the fort, with an authentic Rajasthani spread cooked in the best-quality ghee.
slots.food: Seekh kebabs and the spicy jungle maas, lamb cooked in red chillies.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Mahaveer Rabri Bhandar
slots.text: A fourth-generation hole-in-the-wall in Chandpole Bazar, nationally known for its aloo pyaz sabzi. Open until midnight.
slots.food: Crush the tikkad roti into the sabzi, then finish with laccha rabdi.

days.title: Temple, emerald pool and hot springs

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Tiger Cave Temple
slots.venue: Tiger Cave Temple (Wat Tham Suea): the 1,237-step climb
slots.text: Climb 1,260 steep steps to a cliffside temple, with views over Krabi's forest and the Andaman Sea and a gilded Buddha. No tigers, only macaques.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Emerald Pool
slots.text: A sparkling green pool about two metres deep, fed by thermal springs, in Khao Phra Bang Khram Nature Reserve. An 800-metre path, or a 1,400-metre trail.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Khlong Tom Hot Springs
slots.venue: The natural hot springs (Nam Tok Ron)
slots.text: Warm pools from underground thermal springs, shaded by rainforest and one of the most popular places in the reserve.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Ban Bor Thor Caves
slots.text: Kayak through caves of stalagmites and stalactites, home to ancient paintings left by prehistoric seafarers.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Island hopping
slots.text: Krabi has heaps of white sandy beaches and dreamy islands. Third-party apps like Klook can help with where and how to go.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Romantic Sunset Cruise
slots.text: Sofitel Krabi Phokeethara's cruise drifts into the sunset as the sky turns crimson and pink.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Dragon Crest Mountain
slots.text: A hike of about four kilometres in north Krabi, steep and nearly vertical in places, ending in a rock ledge with views over the gulf.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Tree Top Adventure Krabi
slots.text: A giant zip line through the canopy, plus rope bridges, Tarzan ropes, a flying skateboard and cycling through the trees.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Laem Sak Community
slots.text: A village where Chinese, Muslim migrants and Thai Buddhists live side by side, with a sense of stepping back in time.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Botanic Garden
slots.text: Often compared to Kew Gardens, with tropical plants growing outdoors. Book a private guided tour to learn what each one does.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: L'aventure du Sucre
slots.text: An old factory on the Beau Plan Sugar Estate tells the story of sugarcane, ending with a tasting of different sugars and rums.
slots.food: Le Fangourin on the estate, with local delicacies and rum cocktails.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Chez Tante Athalie
slots.text: An authentic restaurant for the blend of European, Indian, Chinese and Creole food, overlooking grounds dotted with vintage cars.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Le Morne Brabant
slots.text: A rugged Unesco mountain full of caves, once a shelter for runaway slaves and now a symbol of freedom. Book a guide to climb it safely.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Black River Gorges National Park
slots.text: An unspoilt park with about 311 native flowering plants and nine bird species found only here. Take supplies; there's no shop.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: A Creole dinner
slots.text: The food of Mauritius is a blend of the tastes of its former occupiers and of migrant workers from India, China and Africa.

days.title: Zip line, crater lake and Port Louis

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Casela Nature Park
slots.text: An extra-long zip line over canyons and scenery, ending with a splash into the water. Some lines are for singles, some for four.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Ganga Talao
slots.text: A crater lake about 1,800 feet up, with Hindu temples on its banks. Dress modestly and look out for monkeys.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Port Louis and Caudan Waterfront
slots.text: The capital's French colonial-inspired old city, then the relaxed Caudan Waterfront for shopping and dining, and Chinatown.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Göreme Open Air Museum
slots.text: About 150 churches adorned with frescoes, built underground by Christians fleeing persecution. Don't miss Tokalı, Elmalı and Karanlık.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.title: Paşabağları
slots.text: Formerly Monks Valley, with some of Cappadocia's densest fairy chimneys. Saint Simeon's chapel sits inside a three-headed one.

slots.label: Evening
slots.title: Uçhisar Castle
slots.text: The highest point in Cappadocia, with sunset views from Mount Erciyes to Hasan and Melendiz, and Pigeon Valley nearby.

slots.label: Morning
slots.title: Derinkuyu Underground City
